clue.text: Mexican food Chileans 'ad cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests ingredients worked over, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: 'ad is 'had' with its h dropped, spelt AD

explanation.surface: A dish of Mexican food that some Chileans had prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges CHILEANS plus AD from the dialect 'ad.
explanation.definitionFit: These are tortillas rolled round a filling and baked in sauce, a staple dish of Mexico.

clue.text: Every item of fruit's a penny off

indicators.note: off says one piece is taken away from the fruit's name

parts.note: a peach is a single piece of fruit
P is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: Each piece of fruit is marked down by a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes P from PEACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are determiners meaning every one taken individually.

clue.text: Is able to get volunteers to repeat musical performance

parts.note: is able to means can

indicators.note: repeat asks for the volunteers to be written down twice in a row

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's force of volunteer reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: A performer can get volunteers to do a musical show again.
explanation.definitionFit: A choral work with solos and chorus, as by Bach, is a sung piece performed to an audience.

clue.text: Dreadfully noisy cry said to be peculiar behaviour

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests something mangled or done badly, so the words that follow are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreadfully loud scream is said to be someone's odd habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadfully' rearranges NOISY, CRY and SAID; 'said' looks like a homophone signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A quirk or mannerism peculiar to one person is what the longer word names.

clue.text: Flying first class, British entering right part of France

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI with the figure read as a letter

indicators.note: entering says the British letter goes in among the other pieces

parts.note: the Orne is a department of Normandy in France

explanation.surface: Travelling in first class, a Briton arrives in a region of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts B between R and ORNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flying is up in the air, carried aloft.

clue.text: Article portrayed Peter's brother

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
to draw a person is to portray them, past tense drew

explanation.surface: A newspaper article described the brother of Peter.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospels the apostle Simon Peter's brother is the fisherman who became an apostle, Saint Andrew.

clue.text: English company retains hard copy

indicators.note: retains means holds inside, so the company encloses the hard letter

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An English firm keeps a hard copy of its documents.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat someone's words back is to imitate or reproduce them.

clue.text: Slaughter that's new in the era of the motorist?

indicators.note: in places the new letter inside the phrase for the motoring era

parts.note: the age of motoring can be called the car age

explanation.surface: Asks whether road deaths are a new kind of killing peculiar to the motoring age.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful phrase 'car age' for the motoring era.
explanation.definitionFit: Massacre, bloodshed on a large scale.

clue.text: Work hard on the largely mistaken claim of viewer

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: mistaken says these letters are wrongly placed and must be put in another order
largely means most of the word, so its last letter is lost

explanation.surface: Labouring over a largely false claim made by someone watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts THE to TH; 'mistaken' rearranges TH plus CLAIM into THALMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means relating to the eye, and the eye is the organ a person sees with.

clue.text: Nothing's freezing in this

parts.note: on one temperature scale the zero point is exactly where water freezes, so nought degrees means freezing

explanation.surface: Nothing freezes in this place, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests somewhere warm; read 'Nothing' as zero degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: On the Celsius scale water freezes at zero degrees.

clue.text: You'll find it in Perpendicular church

definitions.text: You'll find it in Perpendicular church

indicators.note: says the word sits inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A guide points out a feature of a church in the Perpendicular Gothic style.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Perpendicular' and the start of 'church', and such churches are full of pointed ones: the clue is also its own definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved span over an opening is a basic feature of Gothic church building.

clue.text: It's temporarily erected for pressing reasons

definitions.text: It's temporarily erected for pressing reasons

parts.words: It's temporarily erected for pressing reasons
parts.note: a folding household stand is put up for a while so that clothes can be pressed, then folded away

explanation.surface: Something is put up for a short while because of urgent needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing reasons' suggests urgency; it means pressing laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded folding stand put up while clothes are pressed flat with a hot iron.

clue.text: Spoils of war?

definitions.meaning: to spoil something is to damage or blemish it
the Roman god of war gives his name to the red planet

explanation.surface: Asks about the loot taken in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils of war' reads as plunder; split it into a verb and the war god.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars was the Roman war god, and mars is also a verb meaning blights.

clue.text: Be excessively trying

parts.note: reads as being very tiresome, but means making an attempt that goes too far

explanation.surface: Someone is being extremely tiresome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trying' looks like 'annoying'; read it as 'attempting'.
explanation.definitionFit: To aim or strive beyond one's ability, to try too hard.

clue.text: People responsible for a full house

definitions.text: People responsible for a full house

parts.words: People responsible for a full house
parts.note: sounds like a theatre audience, but the house is the House of Commons, filled by the votes of the public

explanation.surface: Asks who packed out a theatre for a sell-out show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full house' suggests a theatre or poker; it is Parliament, whose seats are filled by voters.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole body of voters chooses the members who fill Parliament's chamber.

clue.text: Inclined to go without right education

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for inclined goes round the right letter

parts.note: something inclined is leaning

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to do without proper schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge gained by study, scholarship.

clue.text: Fantastic runner legally ignoring all the odds

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters leaves only the second, fourth, sixth and so on

explanation.surface: A remarkable athlete who wins fairly despite the long odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odds' sounds like betting; it means the odd-placed letters of 'runner legally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean imaginary or not real, existing only in fantasy.

clue.text: Study of language that could bring one to richer translation

indicators.note: translation turns words into another form, so the letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Learning about language might bring a person to a richer rendering of a text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' rearranges RICHER plus TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of persuasive speech and writing is studied as a branch of language.

clue.text: Salad ingredient — in haste, it's left out

indicators.note: left out says the word that follows is removed

parts.note: celerity is speed or haste
taken as written

explanation.surface: In the rush, an ingredient was forgotten in the salad.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s' is 'is': in CELERITY, IT is left out.
explanation.definitionFit: A crunchy green stalk vegetable eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Learning to get garland for alluring woman

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge or learning
a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland

explanation.surface: Education earns a wreath for a beautiful woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In German legend a siren on the Rhine lured boatmen to their deaths, so the name means a temptress.

clue.text: Press has confused one about exhibit

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the earlier pieces go round the exhibit
confused says the letters of the word before it are mixed up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to hang a picture is to exhibit it

explanation.surface: A muddled person shows something to the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' turns HAS into SHA; with I it goes 'about' HANG.
explanation.definitionFit: To force someone into service, as press gangs did to sailors.

clue.text: Man's masculine policy that limits skirt length

parts.note: he refers to a man
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A man's chauvinist policy of controlling how short skirts are.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom edge of a skirt or dress sets how far down it reaches.

clue.text: Forming a circle around star, light a cigar

definitions.meaning: a ring of light around the sun or another star
a circular chandelier hung in a church

explanation.surface: A ring forms round a star as someone lights up a cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a halo round the sun, a ring-shaped chandelier and a long cigar brand type.

clue.text: It's once or repeatedly mixed as perfume ingredient

indicators.note: mixed says the letters are blended into a new order

parts.note: or written once and then repeated twice more gives three copies

explanation.surface: Something once or often blended to make a perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once or repeatedly' gives OR three times; 'mixed' rearranges ITS plus OROROR.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried root of an iris, smelling of violets, used as a fixative in perfumes.

clue.text: High cost of money once limiting motorway

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so the money goes round the motorway

parts.note: a bob was the old British shilling
M marks a British motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: An old coin's worth enclosing a motorway was expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: A BOB was a shilling, a pre-1971 British coin worth five pence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that costs a bomb, in British slang, is very expensive.

clue.text: Over the canal one can see a divine type

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the canal is read from the bottom up

parts.note: the Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea

explanation.surface: Someone looking over the canal can spot a holy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' turns SUEZ up the column.
explanation.definitionFit: He was king of the Greek gods, a divine being.

clue.text: Associate could be friendly — but not at first

indicators.note: not at first says the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: pally is informal for friendly

explanation.surface: A colleague might be friendly, though not to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not at first' removes P from PALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner or supporter is someone you associate with.

clue.text: Time for us, man, to grab popular gem

parts.note: our means belonging to us

indicators.note: grab means seize and hold, so the man encloses the popular word

parts.note: a man is a male
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A man is told it is time for us to seize a fashionable jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for us' gives the possessive OUR rather than US, and 'popular' is the usual crossword IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A crystalline silicate mineral cut as a gemstone.

clue.text: What's potentially shocking about such corruption?

indicators.note: about signals that the word is turned round

parts.note: a live wire carries current and can give a shock

explanation.surface: Asks what is so shocking about corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocking' looks moral; it is electrical, LIVE, turned 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness and moral corruption.

clue.text: Desire to treat wound for a certain party

parts.note: to fancy is to desire
to dress a wound is to clean and bandage it

explanation.surface: A wish to bandage an injury before some party.
explanation.definitionFit: A party where guests come in costume.
